sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was cyclical rather than smooth: a 22.4% drop in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198], then a 22.1% rebound in FY2021 to $51.0 billion [F6][D251].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume on weaker end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
FY2023 was the margin peak, with operating margin up 6.0pp to 19.3% on favorable price realization and higher volume [F28][D370][P31].
FY2025 reversed part of that, operating margin falling 3.7pp to 16.5% as unfavorable manufacturing costs, largely tariffs, and price realization offset volume [F30][D476][P9].
Power & Energy is now the largest segment at 47.6% of revenue, up from 41.8% in FY2023, and added 5.2pp of FY2025 growth [D753][D757][D759].
Power Generation alone grew 32.5% in FY2025 and contributed 3.9pp, while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D894][D895][D765][D766].
Total sales rose 4.3% to $67.6 billion on higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [F10][D463][P13].
Operating income grew far faster than revenue over the window, at a 28.6% CAGR against 6.4%, but fell 14.7% in FY2025 [F202][F201][D464].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% in FY2025, matching the net income decline, as the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D467][D465][D483].
FY2025 operating margin of 16.5% sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F30][D1123][D1122].
Cost of revenue took 4.2pp off the FY2025 margin, while SG&A and R&D were roughly neutral [D490][D492][D491].
The cost-of-revenue drag reflects unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion, largely higher tariffs [P9].
Net margin fell 3.5pp to 13.1%, a smaller drop than operating margin, as other income of $892 million cushioned the decline [F50][D477][X110].
The effective tax rate rose to 24.0% from 19.7%, working against net margin [D449][D396].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025, above the 1.07x operating-cash-flow-to-net-income peer median [F80][F40][D450][D1154].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% to $8.9 billion, a 13.2% margin against a 11.9% window median [F100][D469][D447][D1129].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion, lifting capex to 1.25x D&A from 0.92x, as investing outflows grew on higher capital expenditures [F90][D470][D452][D399][P3].
Machinery operating cash flow still rose on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes, partly offset by lower profit [P4].
Net debt widened to $26.2 billion in FY2025 from $24.9 billion, as total debt grew 14.1% to $36.2 billion against $10.0 billion of cash [D456][D403][D485][D455][F140].
Net cash of -38.8% of revenue ranks at the 43rd percentile of seven industrials peers, against a peer median of -35.6% [D457][D1151][D1152].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion plus dividends of $2.7 billion used 89.0% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [X140][X150][D459][D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% is the highest of six peers, against a 23.3% peer median [D462][D1155][D1156].
Net debt has now risen two years running, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 to $26.2 billion in FY2025, while debt funded buybacks and higher capex [D350][D456][D485].
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024 to $64.8 billion on lower equipment sales to end users, a one-year dip that FY2025's 4.3% growth reversed [F9][D410][P22][D463].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded, differing from the 10-K by up to 0.06%, so the 10-K figures should be used where precision matters [R3][F40][X20].
Segment revenue members overlap, summing to 219% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so segment lines should not be added together [R6].
Operating margin: a FY2026 print below the 14.3% window median would confirm the tariff-driven compression, while a recovery toward the 20.2% FY2024 high would reverse it [D1123][D1122].
Capex: FY2026 capital expenditures above the FY2025 level of $2.8 billion would keep free cash flow below the 13.2% margin and pressure net debt [F90][D447].
Net cash: a further widening beyond -38.8% of revenue would extend the two-year deterioration in the balance sheet [D457][D456].
